title: Clean and oil the air filter
entry_state: Bike cool, on a stand.
exit_state: Clean, evenly oiled filter sealed in the airbox, seat refitted, service recorded.
completeness: Covers seat removal, filter removal, intake check, washing, oiling, greasing the lip and refitting.

required_tools.name: Foam filter cleaner or warm soapy water

required_parts.name: Spare foam filter
required_parts.purpose: Fit if the old one is torn, hard or shrunken.

prerequisites: Engine stopped and cool.
critical_stop_conditions: Torn, hardened or shrunken foam: do not refit it.
Never clean the filter with gasoline or a low flash-point solvent.
Filter lip not sealing all the way round: do not start the engine.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Clean the air filter after each race (or 2.5 hours), straight away after rain or mud, and more often in dust. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Take off the seat
steps.instruction: Remove the seat.

steps.title: Take the filter out
steps.instruction: Undo the wing bolt and lift the filter out with its frame. Look into the intake duct and carburetor: dirt past the filter means it was not sealing.

branches.label: Dirt past the filter
branches.condition: Clean the intake and carburetor thoroughly before going on, and check the seal extra carefully on refit.

steps.title: Block the intake
steps.instruction: Stuff a clean, lint-free towel into the carburetor opening and wipe the inside of the airbox with a clean damp towel.

steps.title: Wash the foam
steps.instruction: Slide the foam off its frame. Wash it in a high flash-point solvent or hot soapy water, rinse in clear water and squeeze it dry in a towel. Never twist, wring or blow it dry.

branches.label: Foam damaged
branches.condition: Torn, hard or shrunken: fit a new filter and note it.

steps.title: Oil the foam
steps.instruction: Let it dry completely, soak it in good foam filter oil, work the oil in evenly and squeeze out the excess without wringing. Pat the inside with a paper towel.

steps.title: Grease the lip
steps.instruction: Fit the foam back on its frame and grease the filter lip so it seals all round.

steps.title: Take the towel out
steps.instruction: Pull the towel out of the carburetor opening.

steps.title: Fit the filter
steps.instruction: Fit the filter back in its seat and tighten the wing bolt. Run a finger round the edge to check the lip sits flat.

steps.title: Refit the seat
steps.instruction: Refit the seat.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, filter condition and whether a new filter went in.

title: Change the transmission oil
entry_state: Engine warm, bike upright on a stand on level ground.
exit_state: Fresh oil at the middle of the window, drain bolt torqued, no leaks, recorded.
completeness: Covers draining, refilling with the correct amount and type, and the level check.

required_parts.name: Transmission oil
required_parts.purpose: SAE 10W-40 four-stroke oil rated API SG, SH, SJ, SL or SM with JASO MA, MA1 or MA2.

prerequisites: Engine warm; hot oil burns, so wear gloves.
critical_stop_conditions: No oil in the window after refilling: do not ride.
Do not add chemical additives: they upset the wet clutch.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Change the transmission oil every 3 races (or 7.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Warm the oil
steps.instruction: Warm the engine up thoroughly so the oil drains easily and carries the dirt out, then stop it.

steps.title: Drain the oil
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright over a drain pan, remove the oil filler cap, then remove the drain bolt and gasket and let all the oil run out.

branches.label: Metal or milky oil
branches.condition: Metal flakes or milky oil: do not just refill; find the cause and record it.

steps.title: Refit the drain bolt
steps.instruction: Fit the drain bolt with a new gasket. Tighten it to 20 N·m (14.5 ft·lb).

steps.title: Refill
steps.instruction: Pour in 0.5 L (0.53 US qt) of fresh SAE 10W-40 four-stroke oil rated API SG, SH, SJ, SL or SM with JASO MA, MA1 or MA2 and refit the filler cap.

steps.title: Check the level
steps.instruction: Kick the engine over a few times, then with the bike upright and the oil settled, look through the inspection window low on the right side: the level should be in the middle of the window. Remove excess with a syringe or top up with the same oil.
verification: Level in the middle of the window.

steps.title: Check for leaks
steps.instruction: Look round the drain bolt and filler cap for leaks.

steps.title: Record the change
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil and amount used.

title: Check, top up or change the coolant
entry_state: Engine completely cold.
exit_state: Coolant at the bottom of the filler neck, air bled, no leaks, recorded.
completeness: Covers the level check, hose and radiator check, draining, refilling, bleeding and the recheck after a warm-up.

required_parts.name: Coolant
required_parts.purpose: Permanent antifreeze for aluminium engines, mixed half and half with soft or distilled water.

prerequisites: Engine cold. There is no fan on this bike: long idling overheats it.
critical_stop_conditions: Never open the cap on a hot engine.
Coolant on the tyres: wash it off at once.
Never use hard tap water.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the coolant level after each race (or 2.5 hours) and change it when needed. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Position the bike
steps.instruction: With the engine completely cold, hold the bike so the radiator cap is level and uppermost.

steps.title: Open the cap
steps.instruction: Remove the radiator cap in two stages: first to its stop, wait, then press and turn. Never open it on a hot engine.

steps.title: Read the level
steps.instruction: The coolant must reach the bottom of the radiator filler neck. Check the hoses for cracks and loose clamps and the radiator fins for blockage; clean fins with a gentle stream of water only.

branches.label: Low but clean
branches.condition: Top up to the bottom of the filler neck with the same mix and look for the leak.

branches.label: Change due or dirty
branches.condition: Change the coolant.

steps.title: Drain
steps.instruction: Put a pan under the coolant drain plug on the water pump cover and remove it to drain the system.

branches.label: Flakes or brown coolant
branches.condition: White flakes or brown coolant: the system must be flushed. Record it.

steps.title: Refit the drain bolts
steps.instruction: Check the system for damage and loose joints. Refit the drain plug with a new gasket. Tighten the water pump one to 8.8 N·m (78 in·lb).

steps.title: Fill slowly
steps.instruction: Pour coolant (permanent ethylene-glycol antifreeze for aluminium engines, mixed half and half with soft or distilled water) slowly up to the bottom of the filler neck.

steps.title: Bleed the air
steps.instruction: Lean the bike slightly to the right so the filler neck is uppermost and let the air bubble out, tapping the hoses to free trapped bubbles. Top up to the bottom of the neck.
verification: Air bled, level at the neck.

steps.title: Warm up and recheck
steps.instruction: Fit the cap, warm the engine up thoroughly, stop it and let it cool completely. Check the level again and top up if needed.

steps.title: Refit the cap
steps.instruction: Fit the radiator cap fully and look for leaks.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down what you did and the condition of the old coolant.

title: Inspect or replace the spark plug
entry_state: Engine cold.
exit_state: Correct plug fitted and torqued, cap secure, recorded.
completeness: Covers plug removal, reading the plug, gap check, cleaning or replacement and torqueing.
prerequisites: Engine cold.
critical_stop_conditions: Plug will not start by hand: stop and check the thread.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Clean and check the plug after each race (or 2.5 hours) and replace it when needed, checking it every 3 races (or 7.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Clean round the plug
steps.instruction: Clean the cylinder head round the plug cap so no dirt can fall in.

steps.title: Pull off the cap
steps.instruction: Pull the plug cap off by its body, never by the lead.

steps.title: Remove the plug
steps.instruction: Unscrew the plug with a plug socket.

steps.title: Read the plug
steps.instruction: Look at the insulator round the centre electrode. Light brown means the heat range is right; burned black means a hotter plug such as the NGK BR9EG. Clean an oily or sooty plug with a high flash-point solvent and a nylon brush. Replace it if the electrodes are worn or the insulator is cracked.

branches.label: Plug worn
branches.condition: Fit a new NGK BR10EG.

steps.title: Check the gap
steps.instruction: Measure the gap with a wire-type gauge: it must be 0.5 to 0.6 mm (0.020 to 0.024 in.). Correct it by bending the outer electrode only.

steps.title: Fit the plug
steps.instruction: Start the plug by hand, then tighten it to 25.5 N·m (18.8 ft·lb).

steps.title: Refit the cap
steps.instruction: Push the cap fully on and pull lightly to check it has snapped on.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the plug reading and whether a new plug went in.

steps.title: Check the gap
steps.instruction: Check the electrode is not worn or burned back; this plug is not regapped, so fit a new one if it is worn.

title: Check and adjust the clutch cable
entry_state: Engine stopped.
exit_state: Clutch lever free play correct, locknuts tight, clutch tested, recorded.
completeness: Covers checking lever free play and adjusting at the lever and at the cable adjuster.
prerequisites: Engine stopped.
critical_stop_conditions: Clutch slips or will not release: do not ride.
Outer cable not seated in its fitting: it can drop in later and leave too much play.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check and adjust the clutch after each race (or 2.5 hours). Free play grows as the cable stretches and the plates wear. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Check the free play
steps.instruction: Pull the lever gently until you feel the cable take up. There must be a small, definite amount of free play at the lever end before the clutch starts to work.

branches.label: Free play correct
branches.condition: Go to the test.

steps.title: Adjust at the lever
steps.instruction: Slide back the dust cover, loosen the locknut and turn the adjuster until the free play is right, then tighten the locknut. Make sure the outer cable is fully seated in its fitting.

steps.title: Adjust further down the cable
steps.instruction: If the lever adjuster runs out, turn it all the way in and lock it, then loosen the locknut or nuts on the cable adjuster lower down and turn them until the free play is right. Tighten them.

steps.title: Test the clutch
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check the clutch does not slip and releases fully. Slide the dust cover back into place.

steps.title: Record the check
steps.instruction: Write down the free play and any adjustment.

title: Check the carburetor jetting baseline and set the idle

Engine pinging or running hot after a leaner change: go back richer at once.

steps.title: Compare with what is fitted

title: Check, adjust and lubricate the drive chain
entry_state: Bike on a stand with the rear wheel off the ground, engine stopped.
exit_state: Chain slack set at its tightest point, wheel aligned, axle torqued, chain lubricated, recorded.
completeness: Covers finding the tightest point, measuring slack, adjusting with wheel alignment, axle nut inspection and torque, wear and sprocket checks and lubrication.

required_tools.name: Stand that lifts the rear wheel
Wrenches for the axle nut and adjusters

required_parts.name: Cotter pin
required_parts.purpose: New cotter pin for the rear axle nut every time it is removed.

prerequisites: Engine stopped; keep fingers away from the sprockets while turning the wheel.
critical_stop_conditions: Damaged rollers, loose pins, kinks or hooked sprocket teeth: replace the chain and sprockets before riding.
No new cotter pin in the axle nut: do not ride.
Chain too tight is as dangerous as too loose: it can break.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check and adjust the chain after each race (or 2.5 hours), lubricate it after each race (or 2.5 hours) and check it for wear every 5 races (or 12.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand so the rear wheel turns freely.

steps.title: Find the tightest point
steps.instruction: Turn the rear wheel slowly and push up on the chain at several points: chains wear unevenly, so find where it is tightest and measure there.

steps.title: Measure the slack
steps.instruction: At the tightest point, push the upper run of the chain up just behind the rear end of the chain slipper and measure the gap between the bottom of the chain and the swingarm at the end of the slipper. Compare it with your bike's standard chain slack range. In wet, muddy conditions run it toward the loose side, because packed mud tightens the chain.

branches.label: Slack in range
branches.condition: Slack already correct: go on to the wear check.

steps.title: Loosen the axle
steps.instruction: Pull out the cotter pin, then loosen the rear axle nut and both chain adjuster locknuts.

steps.title: Set the slack and alignment
steps.instruction: Turn both adjusting bolts by the same amount until the slack is right. If the chain is too tight, back both bolts out evenly and push the wheel forward. Keep the notch or rear edge of each adjuster on the same swingarm mark on both sides so the wheel stays straight.
verification: Slack set, both adjusters on the same mark.

steps.title: Check the axle nut
steps.instruction: Look at the rear axle nut. If it is damaged, fit a new one.

steps.title: Tighten everything
steps.instruction: Tighten both chain adjuster locknuts, then the rear axle nut to 78 N·m (58 ft·lb). Fit a new cotter pin through the axle and bend its ends.

steps.title: Recheck the slack
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel, measure the slack again at the tightest point and readjust if needed. Check the rear brake works and does not drag.

steps.title: Check chain and sprocket wear
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel and look for damaged rollers, loose pins or links and stiff spots. Look at the teeth on both sprockets: hooked, worn or broken teeth mean new sprockets, and a new chain should always go on with good sprockets. Check the chain slipper on the swingarm and the chain guide for wear. Check the rear sprocket every 5 races (or 12.5 hours).
verification: Chain, sprockets, slipper and guide inspected.

branches.label: Worn or damaged parts
branches.condition: Replace the worn parts before riding and record what was changed.

steps.title: Lubricate the chain
steps.instruction: Apply a good drive chain lubricant to the sides of the rollers so it soaks into the rollers and bushings, then wipe off the excess. Lube it after any wet ride or whenever it looks dry.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the slack before and after, the alignment mark used and the condition of the chain and sprockets.

title: Check the brake pads and brake fluid
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Pads and fluid checked, topped up if needed, brakes firm and free, recorded.
completeness: Covers fluid level in both reservoirs, topping up, pad lining checks, hose checks, lever position and a function test.
excluded: Bleeding or changing the brake fluid

required_parts.name: Brake fluid
required_parts.purpose: Fresh fluid of the grade marked on each reservoir cap, from a sealed container, only if topping up.

prerequisites: Engine stopped.
critical_stop_conditions: Spongy lever or pedal: air in the system; do not ride, have it bled.
Pad lining worn to the service limit on either pad: replace both pads in that caliper as a set before riding.
Brake fluid strips paint: wipe any drip off at once.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the brake pads every 5 races (or 12.5 hours) and the brake fluid level every 3 races (or 7.5 hours); the fluid is changed every 2 years by someone with bleeding equipment. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Check the front fluid
steps.instruction: Turn the handlebar so the front reservoir is level. The fluid must be above the lower level line.

steps.title: Check the rear fluid
steps.instruction: With the bike upright and the rear reservoir level, check its fluid against its level marks.

branches.label: Either level low
branches.condition: Below the mark: look for a leak first, then top up.

branches.label: Both levels fine
branches.condition: Go on to the pads.

steps.title: Top up
steps.instruction: Clean round the cap, open the reservoir and add fresh fluid of the grade marked on the cap up to the upper level line or step inside the reservoir. Never mix brands or types; if you do not know what is in there, have the whole system flushed. Refit the cap snugly.

steps.title: Check the pads
steps.instruction: Look into each caliper with a torch at the lining left on both pads. If either lining on a caliper is worn to its service limit, replace both pads in that caliper as a set.
verification: Lining thickness checked on all four pads.

branches.label: Pads worn
branches.condition: Lining at or below the limit: replace the pads before riding and record it.

steps.title: Check hoses and fittings
steps.instruction: Look for fluid round the master cylinders, calipers and hose fittings, and for cracks or chafing on the hoses.

steps.title: Set the lever
steps.instruction: Turn the front lever adjuster to put the lever where the rider likes it.

steps.title: Test the brakes
steps.instruction: Pump the lever and pedal: both must feel firm. Spin each wheel: it must turn freely without drag when released.

branches.label: Soft or spongy
branches.condition: Spongy feel means air in the line: do not ride; have the brake bled and record it.

steps.title: Record the check
steps.instruction: Write down the fluid levels, pad condition and anything you found.

title: Release built-up air from the fork
entry_state: Front wheel off the ground, fork fully extended.
exit_state: Both fork legs back at atmospheric pressure, screws refitted.
completeness: Covers lifting the front wheel, opening and closing the pressure relief screw on each fork leg, and the fork tube check.

required_tools.name: Stand that lifts the front wheel

prerequisites: Do it before every race or practice session: air pressure builds up in the fork as it works and stiffens it.
critical_stop_conditions: Never add air to make the fork stiffer: it is designed to run at atmospheric pressure.
Oil spitting from the screw hole or wet fork tubes: have the seals checked.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and how the fork felt at the end of the last ride. Clean and inspect the fork after each race (or 2.5 hours).

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put a stand under the frame so the front wheel is off the ground and the fork hangs fully extended. Take off the number plate if it is in the way.

steps.title: Open the relief screws
steps.instruction: Remove the pressure relief screw on the top plug of each fork leg and let the trapped air hiss out until the pressure equalises (standard is atmospheric (0 kPa, 0 psi)).

steps.title: Refit the screws
steps.instruction: Refit the screws with their O-rings and tighten them to 1.3 N·m (12 in·lb).

steps.title: Clean the fork tubes
steps.instruction: Wipe mud and dust off the inner tubes so it cannot damage the seals, and look for oil leaks or scratches on the tubes.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Note that the air was released and anything you saw on the fork tubes.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the top plug and slide the outer tube down. title: Set the suspension back to the standard baseline
entry_state: Bike on a stand, suspension clean.
exit_state: Clickers at standard, springs, preload and fork height checked, pressures set, baseline recorded.
completeness: Covers recording the old settings, standard clicker positions, spring, fork height and preload checks, tyre pressures and a sag reference.
prerequisites: Suspension clean so the adjusters can be counted.
critical_stop_conditions: Never force an adjuster past its seated position.
Left and right fork legs set differently: do not ride.

steps.title: Record the current settings
steps.instruction: Count and write down every current clicker and preload setting before changing anything, then put each adjuster back.

steps.title: Set fork rebound
steps.instruction: The rebound adjuster is on each fork top plug. On this fork the seated position is with the adjuster turned fully counterclockwise: turn it that way gently until it stops, then turn it back 3 clicks clockwise from there. Set both legs the same.

steps.title: Set shock rebound
steps.instruction: The rebound adjuster is at the bottom of the shock. Seat it gently clockwise, then turn it 1 1/2 turns counterclockwise.

steps.title: Check the shock preload
steps.instruction: Measure from the centre of the upper shock mounting hole to the spring preload adjusting nut. Standard is 79.6 mm (3.13 in.).

branches.label: Not at standard
branches.condition: Different: set it with the shock preload guide.

steps.title: Set tyre pressures
steps.instruction: With the tyres cold, set both within 80 kPa (11 psi) to 100 kPa (14 psi).

steps.title: Measure sag for reference
steps.instruction: With the rider in full gear on the pegs, measure how far the rear sinks from fully extended and write it down as your reference.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the pressures, the sag and the track conditions.

steps.instruction: Put the bike on its side stand, remove the seat and both side covers, loosen the air intake duct clamp, remove the airbox bolts and take off the rear frame together with the airbox.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Measure from the centre of the upper shock mounting hole to the adjusting nut. Standard is 79.6 mm (3.13 in.); stay within 75.6 to 83.6 mm (2.98 to 3.30 in.).

steps.title: Turn the adjusting nut
steps.instruction: Turn the adjusting nut with a hook wrench: down the shock adds preload, up removes it. Measure again until it is where you want it.

steps.instruction: Tighten the locknut firmly against the adjusting nut and move the spring up and down to check it is seated.

title: Do the pre-ride check
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine cold.
exit_state: Every daily item checked, faults put right or recorded.
completeness: Covers the daily walk-round of fluids, filter, controls, brakes, chain, wheels, steering, suspension and fasteners.
prerequisites: A few minutes before every ride.
critical_stop_conditions: Throttle that does not snap shut: do not start the engine.
Spongy brakes or any fuel leak: do not ride.

steps.title: Record the date
steps.instruction: Write down the date and the hours before the ride.

steps.title: Fuel
steps.instruction: Fill with fresh fuel premixed with two-stroke oil at 32 : 1, shaken well, and check the tank cap breather hose is in place.

steps.title: Engine fluids
steps.instruction: Look in the transmission oil window: the level must be in the middle of the window with the bike upright. With the engine cold, check the coolant reaches the bottom of the filler neck, the radiator cap is fully on and nothing leaks.
verification: Oil and coolant correct, no leaks.

steps.title: Air filter
steps.instruction: Make sure the air filter is clean, oiled and sealed, and the airbox cover or seat is secure.

steps.title: Spark plug and head
steps.instruction: Make sure the spark plug cap is pushed fully home.

steps.title: Controls
steps.instruction: Twist the throttle: it must snap shut by itself in every handlebar position without the cables binding. Pull the clutch lever: it must have its small free play and work smoothly. Check the engine stop button works.
verification: Throttle, clutch and stop button working.

steps.title: Brakes
steps.instruction: Pump the front lever and rear pedal: both must feel firm with no fluid leaks.

steps.title: Chain and sprockets
steps.instruction: Check the chain slack at its tightest point, oil the chain if it is dry and look for worn or damaged sprocket teeth.

steps.title: Wheels and tyres
steps.instruction: Set both tyres, cold, within 80 kPa (11 psi) to 100 kPa (14 psi) to suit the track. Check the valve caps are on, the tyres are not damaged and no spokes are loose.

steps.title: Steering and suspension
steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock: smooth but not loose. Pump the fork and the rear end: both must move smoothly with no oil on the fork tubes or shock.

steps.title: Frame, exhaust and fasteners
steps.instruction: Look over the frame and exhaust for cracks or damage, make sure the fuel tank is mounted securely with no fuel leaks, and check that nuts and bolts are tight.

steps.title: Record anything found
steps.instruction: Write down anything you adjusted or that needs attention before the next ride.

title: Wash the bike and do the after-wash check
entry_state: Bike back from riding, engine stopped.
exit_state: Clean, dry, lubricated bike, inspected and recorded.
completeness: Covers safe washing, drying, running the bike dry, chain and pivot lubrication and the after-ride inspection.
prerequisites: Engine and exhaust cool.
critical_stop_conditions: Water inside the airbox: dry it and service the filter before starting.
Brakes not biting after the wash: dry them before riding at speed.

steps.title: Record the date
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. General lubrication is due after each race (or 2.5 hours).

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.instruction: Let the engine and exhaust cool down before any water touches them.

steps.title: Protect the openings
steps.instruction: Make sure the airbox is closed and plug the muffler outlet. Keep water away from the air intake, carburetor, brakes, electrics and fuel tank opening.

steps.title: Wash gently
steps.instruction: Rinse off loose dirt with cold water from a garden hose, then wash with a mild neutral detergent and a soft sponge. Do not use a pressure washer: it drives water past seals and into electrics, and can flatten the radiator fins. Keep degreaser off seals, brake pads and tyres.

steps.title: Rinse and dry
steps.instruction: Rinse off all detergent with clean water and dry the bike with a soft cloth, looking for cracks, chips and damage as you go. Wash any fuel, brake fluid or coolant off paint and plastic straight away.

steps.title: Unplug the outlets
steps.instruction: Take the plug out of the muffler outlet and check the airbox is dry inside.

steps.title: Run it dry
steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle for several minutes so the heat dries damp areas. Ride slowly and use both brakes several times to dry the pads.
verification: Engine run, brakes dried and working.

steps.title: Lubricate the chain
steps.instruction: Lubricate the drive chain so it does not rust.

steps.title: General lubrication
steps.instruction: Oil the clutch and front brake lever pivots, the shift pedal, rear brake pedal and footpeg pivots, and lubricate the control cables.

steps.title: After-ride inspection
steps.instruction: Check the air filter, brakes, fork tubes and shock shaft for dirt and damage, and wipe the fork tubes clean so mud cannot damage the seals.

steps.title: Record anything found
steps.instruction: Write down anything that needs attention before the next ride.
